text: The Navigator handles where to anchor for the night and assessing whether an anchorage is safe, using the pilot book, currents, and weather.
The Navigator handles tidal currents at passes and gates, slack timing, and what the current is doing nearby.
The Navigator handles tide heights and the next high and low water.
The Navigator handles wind and marine weather forecasts, buoy observations, and offshore passage weather.
The Navigator handles yacht club outstations and moorage availability for overnight stops.
The Navigator handles the rules of the road, right of way, and required sound and light signals.
The Engineer handles battery state of charge, house and start banks, and electrical questions.
The Engineer handles fuel, water, holding and black water tank levels.
The Engineer handles depth under the keel and sounder readings.
The Engineer handles active alarms, what an alarm means, and what to do about it, using vessel equipment knowledge.
The Engineer handles questions about specific onboard equipment: make, model, service intervals, and how a device works.
The Logbook keeper records notable moments and answers questions about past log entries and the sea day.
